actions.text: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
Motion to reconsider laid on the table Agreed to without objection.
On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
Passed/agreed to in House: On motion to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended Agreed to by voice vote.
Considered as unfinished business. (consideration: CR H4079)

At the conclusion of debate, the chair put the question on the motion to suspend the rules. Mr. Gill (TX) objected to the vote on the grounds that a quorum was not present. Further proceedings on the motion were postponed. The point of no quorum was considered as withdrawn.
DEBATE - The House proceeded with forty minutes of debate on H.R. 8340.
Considered under suspension of the rules. (consideration: CR H3931-3933; text: CR H3931-3932)
Mr. Gill (TX) moved to suspend the rules and pass the bill, as amended.
Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 40 - 0.
Committee Consideration and Mark-up Session Held
Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.

committees.name: Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee

dimensions.assessment: Directly affects financial management personnel, Chief Financial Officers, and administrative operations across all executive agencies.
dimensions.evidence: It shall be the duty and responsibility of each agency Chief Financial Officer to oversee and, unless specified otherwise in law, provide leadership in the areas of budget formulation

dimensions.assessment: Modifies agency administrative duties, planning cycles, and internal control evaluations without altering citizen-facing program benefits.
dimensions.evidence: The head of each executive agency shall annually assess and make a conclusion on the effectiveness of the internal controls of the executive agency over financial reporting

dimensions.assessment: Revises internal reporting and planning requirements within existing agency structures, with no specific new federal appropriations or spending figures stated.
Amends Title 31 of the United States Code to change government-wide financial management plans from 5-year to 4-year cycles and adds statutory duties for agency CFOs.
dimensions.evidence: The bill requires the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to take certain actions to improve financial management systems across the federal government and expands the responsibilities of federal agency Chief Financial Officers (CFOs).

dimensions.assessment: Imposes permanent statutory amendments to federal financial management and four-year planning cycles.
dimensions.evidence: The bill requires OMB to submit a four-year governmentwide financial management plan to Congress within 12 months of enactment and thereafter with the budget

missing_information: Any potential administrative cost estimates for carrying out the expanded CFO duties and four-year plans.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill modifies government-wide financial management plans and expands Chief Financial Officer duties across federal agencies, establishing new reporting and internal control assessments.
